newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey aims balanced 1997 budget, real wage rise.
newsitem.headline: Turkey aims balanced 1997 budget, real wage rise.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Tuesday his Islamist-led coalition government will draw up a zero-deficit budget for next year which aims to grant real wage hikes to public employees.
"Our government is coming up with the aim of a balanced budget and it will realise this goal," Erbakan told his party's parliamentary group meeting.
The government expects the 1996 budget deficit to overshoot 1,300 trillion lira, sharply up from 317 trillion last year.
"Under the new budget, welfare levels of civil servants, workers and craftsmen will be raised. A real rise above inflation will be given," Erbakan said.
He said the budget would also boost investment and improve the domestic defence industry.
Economists and economy officials say the government's plan for a zero-budget deficit and real wage rises to public employees is not realistic.
"To achieve a zero-deficit goal, Turkey must not pay any new interests on domestic and foreign debts next year. This is not possible," said a senior economy official, who declined to be named.
"This is just a political manoeuvre and, maybe, a sign of a preparation for an early election," the official said.

Economists say Erbakan's approach to the 1997 budget may kill the possibility of a stand-by accord with the International Monetary Fund, which the coalition government's junior partner True Path Party of Tansu Ciller has urged for.
State Minister Ufuk Soylemez had earlier said the IMF might give financial support to Turkey's stability programme.
Officials say an IMF team is expected to come to Ankara for talks on a stand-by arrangement to rescue the country's troubled economy from big public deficits and high inflation.
Turkey is expected to draft the 1997 budget this month. According to the budget law, parliament must debate and approve it by the end of the year.
